headline: High risk of git-state conflicts and cascading misautomation; prompt-injection and leakage are lower because the pair lacks a direct shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider can read and write repo files and Prefect can orchestrate workflows, but no direct shared channel, MCP bridge, or clipboard path is documented. The only plausible bridge is manual file handoff through the shared repo, so injection is possible but not default and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies Prefect-generated text into Aider prompts or repo files, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF Prefect writes attacker-controlled content into shared files that Aider later reads, Aider may follow it as instructions.
mitigations: Keep Aider and Prefect on separate repos or branches.
Review any workflow text before pasting it into Aider.
Add a short prompt prefix telling Aider to ignore instructions in files.
Use a manual approval step before Aider edits files from Prefect outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history, while Prefect only exposes workflow metadata and has broad network egress. There is no documented shared workspace or authenticated shared principal, so leakage is not default; however, manual transfer of repo content into Prefect or logs could expose code snippets.
conditions: IF Aider outputs source code into Prefect task logs, code may leak beyond the repo.
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace by the operator, file contents can cross boundaries.
mitigations: Do not pass source files into Prefect task parameters.
Redact code from workflow logs.
Run Prefect with minimal logging for tasks that mention repo content.
Keep secrets out of git-tracked files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shared_state_with_other_instances via a shared git repo; Prefect can also drive networked automation. Concurrent writes to the same repo or workflow artifacts can race and corrupt state. Because the shared git repo is explicit and no locking is documented, the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF Prefect and Aider target the same git repository concurrently, commit and file-write races can occur.
IF Prefect triggers repeated runs while Aider is editing, state divergence becomes likely.
mitigations: Serialize access to the shared repo.
Use separate branches per run.
Pause Prefect jobs while Aider is committing.
Add a pre-commit check for unexpected diffs.
requires-engineering: add repository locking in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate code changes and Prefect can orchestrate downstream automation, so Aider output may become operational input. Prefect is not documented here as verifying Aider’s claims before acting, but the pair does not show direct destructive actions by default, so medium fits the default cascade risk.
conditions: IF Prefect consumes Aider-produced files or summaries without validation, incorrect code or metadata can propagate.
IF Prefect schedules deployments or jobs based on Aider output, errors can cascade into downstream systems.
mitigations: Require human review of Aider output before Prefect uses it.
Add schema validation on any Aider-produced artifact.
Compare generated diffs against expected paths.
Limit Prefect to read-only inspection tasks until validated.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles source code and git history, while Prefect handles workflow metadata; no PHI, EU PII, or residency mismatch is stated. The pair still has a compliance gap because Aider may send prompts to configured model providers, but the profile does not show a specific regulated data class crossing into Prefect.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in git-tracked files and Aider sends those contents to a model provider, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF Prefect logs workflow metadata containing regulated identifiers, retention policy mismatches may arise.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from repos used by Aider.
Disable verbose logging in Prefect for sensitive workflows.
Review model-provider data handling settings.
Use synthetic data in integration tests.
